subject.title: fix: models fallbacks --agent silently edits global defaults instead of the agent

question: When --agent names an agent that currently inherits agents.defaults.model, should fallback add/remove/clear materialize a per-agent override or intentionally edit the inherited global defaults?
rationale: Both behaviors are implementable and current helper precedent favors effective-value writes, but the CLI flag communicates a targeted operation while global mutation affects unrelated agents; repository evidence does not establish which contract maintainers want permanently.

options.title: Materialize Agent Override
options.body: Always write agents.list[].model.fallbacks when --agent is explicit, preserving global defaults and making the command target match operator intent.

options.title: Keep Effective-Owner Writes
options.body: Retain global writes for inheriting agents, but explicitly approve the cross-agent effect and preserve tests and documentation that make it unmistakable.

recommendation.title: Materialize Agent Override
recommendation.body: Always write agents.list[].model.fallbacks when --agent is explicit, preserving global defaults and making the command target match operator intent.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged per-agent defaults and safe-fallback work is the closest historical source for deciding the intended ownership contract.
